column1: Glass, which has been made since the time of the Mesopotamians and Egyptians, is little more than a mixture of sand, soda ash and lime.
column2: 从美索不达米亚人和古埃及人的时代起，人们就一直在制造玻璃。玻璃的主要成分不过是沙子、纯碱和石灰。
column3: since the time of|自……时代以来

column1: When heated to about 1500 degrees Celsius (°C) this becomes a molten mass that hardens when slowly cooled.
column2: 混合物加热到约1500摄氏度时会熔成一团，缓慢冷却后便会变硬。

column1: The first successful method for making clear, flat glass involved spinning.
column2: 最早成功制出透明平板玻璃的方法用到了旋转成形。

column1: This method was very effective as the glass had not touched any surfaces between being soft and becoming hard, so it stayed perfectly unblemished, with a ‘fire finish’.
column2: 这种方法很有效。玻璃在由软变硬的过程中没有接触任何其他表面，因此表面始终光洁无瑕，保留了火抛光形成的光泽。
column10: fire finish|n. 火抛光形成的光洁表面

column1: However, the process took a long time and was labour intensive.
column2: 不过，这道工序既费时又耗费人力。
column4: took a long time|耗时很久
column5: labour intensive|adj. 耗费大量人力的

column1: Nevertheless, demand for flat glass was very high and glassmakers across the world were looking for a method of making it continuously.
column2: 尽管如此，平板玻璃的需求量仍然很大，世界各地的玻璃制造商都在寻找连续生产它的方法。

column1: The first continuous ribbon process involved squeezing molten glass through two hot rollers, similar to an old mangle.
column2: 最早的连续玻璃带生产工艺是把熔融玻璃从两个热轧辊之间挤过去，跟老式衣物轧水机的原理相似。

column1: This allowed glass of virtually any thickness to be made non-stop, but the rollers would leave both sides of the glass marked, and these would then need to be ground and polished.
column2: 这样几乎任何厚度的玻璃都可以连续生产。但轧辊会在玻璃的两面留下痕迹，两面随后都得研磨、抛光。

column1: This part of the process rubbed away around 20 per cent of the glass, and the machines were very expensive.
column2: 这道工序会磨掉约20%的玻璃，所用的机器也十分昂贵。

column1: The float process for making flat glass was invented by Alistair Pilkington.
column2: 制造平板玻璃的浮法工艺由阿利斯泰尔·皮尔金顿发明。

column1: This process allows the manufacture of clear, tinted and coated glass for buildings, and clear and tinted glass for vehicles.
column2: 这项工艺既能生产建筑用的透明玻璃、着色玻璃和镀膜玻璃，也能生产车辆用的透明玻璃和着色玻璃。

column1: Pilkington had been experimenting with improving the melting process, and in 1952 he had the idea of using a bed of molten metal to form the flat glass, eliminating altogether the need for rollers within the float bath.
column2: 皮尔金顿一直在试验如何改进熔化工艺。1952年，他想到用一层熔融金属来使平板玻璃成形，这样就完全不必在浮槽内使用轧辊。

column1: The metal had to melt at a temperature less than the hardening point of glass (about 600°C), but could not boil at a temperature below the temperature of the molten glass (about 1500°C).
column2: 这种金属的熔点必须低于玻璃的硬化温度（约600摄氏度），但它在低于熔融玻璃温度（约1500摄氏度）时不能沸腾。

column1: The best metal for the job was tin.
column2: 最适合这个用途的金属是锡。
column5: for the job|用于这一用途

column1: The rest of the concept relied on gravity, which guaranteed that the surface of the molten metal was perfectly flat and horizontal.
column2: 这一构想的其余部分依靠重力。重力能确保熔融金属的表面完全平整，并保持水平。

column1: Consequently, when pouring molten glass onto the molten tin, the underside of the glass would also be perfectly flat.
column2: 因此，熔融玻璃浇在熔融的锡液上时，玻璃的底面也会完全平整。

column1: If the glass were kept hot enough, it would flow over the molten tin until the top surface was also flat, horizontal and perfectly parallel to the bottom surface.
column2: 只要玻璃保持足够高的温度，它就会在锡液上流动、铺展，直到上表面也变得平整、水平，并与底面完全平行。

column1: Once the glass cooled to 604°C or less it was too hard to mark and could be transported out of the cooling zone by rollers.
column2: 玻璃一旦冷却至604摄氏度或以下，就已硬到不会留下压痕，可以用辊轮将它送出冷却区。
column6: too hard to mark|硬到不会留下压痕

column1: The glass settled to a thickness of six millimetres because of surface tension interactions between the glass and the tin.
column2: 由于玻璃与锡之间的表面张力相互作用，玻璃的厚度最终稳定在六毫米。

column1: By fortunate coincidence, 60 per cent of the flat glass market at that time was for six-millimetre glass.
column2: 碰巧，当时平板玻璃市场上有60%的需求就是六毫米厚的玻璃。

column1: Pilkington built a pilot plant in 1953 and by 1955 he had convinced his company to build a full-scale plant.
column2: 皮尔金顿于1953年建了一座试验工厂，到1955年已说服公司兴建一座工业规模的工厂。
column7: full-scale plant|n. 工业规模的工厂

column1: However, it took 14 months of non-stop production, costing the company £100,000 a month, before the plant produced any usable glass.
column2: 然而，工厂连续生产了14个月，每月耗费公司10万英镑，才生产出可用的玻璃。

column1: Furthermore, once they succeeded in making marketable flat glass, the machine was turned off for a service to prepare it for years of continuous production.
column2: 而且，他们一制出可以上市销售的平板玻璃，就停机检修，为此后数年的连续生产做准备。

column1: When it started up again it took another four months to get the process right again.
column2: 机器重新启动后，又花了四个月才把工艺重新调好。
column5: get the process right|把工艺调好

column1: They finally succeeded in 1959 and there are now float plants all over the world, with each able to produce around 1000 tons of glass every day, non-stop for around 15 years.
column2: 他们终于在1959年取得成功。如今世界各地都有浮法玻璃厂，每家每天可生产约1000吨玻璃，可连续生产约15年。
column6: all over the world|世界各地

column1: Float plants today make glass of near optical quality.
column2: 如今，浮法玻璃厂生产的玻璃，品质已接近光学玻璃。
column4: near optical quality|接近光学玻璃的品质

column1: Several processes - melting, refining, homogenising - take place simultaneously in the 2000 tonnes of molten glass in the furnace.
column2: 炉内装有2000吨熔融玻璃，熔化、澄清和均化等几个过程在其中同时进行。

column1: They occur in separate zones in a complex glass flow driven by high temperatures.
column2: 这些过程分别发生在不同区域；高温驱动玻璃液流动，形成复杂的流态。
column7: glass flow|n. 玻璃液的流动

column1: It adds up to a continuous melting process, lasting as long as 50 hours, that delivers glass smoothly and continuously to the float bath, and from there to a coating zone and finally a heat treatment zone, where stresses formed during cooling are relieved.
column2: 这些工序合在一起，形成一个耗时可长达50小时的连续熔化过程。这一过程将玻璃液平稳、连续地送入浮槽，再送至镀膜区，最后送入热处理区，冷却过程中形成的应力在这里得到消除。
column11: heat treatment zone|n. 热处理区

column1: The principle of float glass is unchanged since the 1950s.
column2: 浮法玻璃的原理自20世纪50年代以来一直没有改变。

column1: However, the product has changed dramatically, from a single thickness of 6.8 mm to a range from sub-millimetre to 25 mm, from a ribbon frequently marred by inclusions and bubbles to almost optical perfection.
column2: 不过，产品本身已大不相同。厚度起初只有6.8毫米一种，如今从不足1毫米到25毫米都有。玻璃带原先常因夹杂物和气泡而有瑕疵，如今在光学质量上已近乎完美。
column12: optical perfection|n. 完美的光学质量

column1: To ensure the highest quality, inspection takes place at every stage.
column2: 为确保最高质量，每道工序都要进行检验。

column1: Occasionally, a bubble is not removed during refining, a sand grain refuses to melt, a tremor in the tin puts ripples into the glass ribbon.
column2: 偶尔会有气泡在澄清过程中没有排出，或有一粒沙子始终没有熔化，又或是锡液的轻微震动使玻璃带出现波纹。

column1: Automated on-line inspection does two things.
column2: 生产线上的自动检验有两项作用。
column4: on-line|adj. 在生产线上进行的

column1: Firstly, it reveals process faults upstream that can be corrected.
column2: 第一，它能发现上游工序中可以纠正的问题。

column1: Inspection technology allows more than 100 million measurements a second to be made across the ribbon, locating flaws the unaided eye would be unable to see.
column2: 这项检测技术每秒能在整条玻璃带上进行超过一亿次测量，从而找出肉眼看不见的缺陷。

column1: Secondly, it enables computers downstream to steer cutters around flaws.
column2: 第二，这项技术使下游工序的计算机能够控制切割器，绕开缺陷部位。

column1: Float glass is sold by the square metre, and at the final stage computers translate customer requirements into patterns of cuts designed to minimise waste.
column2: 浮法玻璃按平方米出售。到了最后一道工序，计算机会把客户的要求转化为切割方案，以尽量减少浪费。
column4: by the square metre|按平方米
column5: final stage|n. 最后一道工序
